column1: # Sample sheet - EDIT THIS to describe your experiment, then delete these
# comment lines or leave them (lines starting with # are ignored).
# One row per FINAL demultiplexed sample (i.e. per biological specimen).
# If you pooled specimens and separated them with hashtags, that is several
# rows sharing one pool.
# Columns (tab-separated, order matters):
#   pool         Name of the sequencing pool / Cell Ranger run this sample
#                belongs to. One cellranger multi job is created per unique
#                pool. If you did not pool, use one pool per sample.
#   pool_prefix  The prefix of the fastq filenames for this pool, as delivered.
#                For a file named 1-GEX_S1_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz the prefix is 1.
#                Every sample in a pool shares the same prefix.
#   hashtag_id   The hashtag that identifies this sample within its pool. Must
#                match an id in 01_preprocessing/02_cellranger/refs/feature_ref.csv.
#                Set to NA if USE_HASHTAG_DEMUX=false in config.env.
#   sample_id    Unique name for this sample. This becomes the Cell Ranger
#                per-sample output directory name, so keep it filesystem-safe:
#                letters, numbers and underscores only.
#   group        The analysis group this sample belongs to. The per-sample R
#                pipeline is run once per group, and groups are then combined
#                by the integrated analysis. Often this equals pool, but it can
#                differ (e.g. group by tissue while pooling by batch).
#   condition    The experimental condition, used as the main comparison
#                variable in differential expression. Keep the exact same
#                spelling across groups.
#   replicate    Replicate number within condition and group.
# The example below is a two-pool, four-hashtag design: two conditions with
# two replicates each, in each of two tissues. Replace it entirely.
